---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Hard Capital Stock Under Demand Uncertainty
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(VOL(GROWTH(sale, 1), 5)), RANK(RATIO(ppent, ADD(ppent, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)))))
HYPOTHESIS: What matters under volatile demand is not only this year's allocation decision but the accumulated stock of sunk physical capital relative to flexible knowledge capital, because a firm already locked into plant cannot contract when demand disappoints.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Irreversible Capacity Under Demand Uncertainty is now the archive's best joint result (fmb -2.62, alpha -5.2%, t -3.74), and the first question for consolidation is whether the effect is a flow decision or a state of commitment; this replaces the one-year investment mix with the corresponding capital-stock composition while holding the uncertainty leg fixed. A stock formulation is also mechanically more stable than a single-year capex ratio, so it should raise coverage-quality and the cross-sectional slope if the commitment interpretation is right.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Irreversible Acquisitions Under Demand Uncertainty
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(VOL(GROWTH(sale, 1), 5)), RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(aqc, 0), 3), ADD(TS_SUM(capx, 3), ADD(TS_SUM(COALESCE(aqc, 0), 3), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3))))))
HYPOTHESIS: Investment types differ in reversibility — research can be throttled, plant can at least be run down, but an acquisition is instantly sunk including its integration cost — so the uncertainty penalty should be strongest for firms that allocate their budget to deals.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This is the one crossing that unites the archive's two largest-alpha families, the acquisition channel (alphas of -4.5% to -5.4%) and the demand-uncertainty channel, under a single testable ordering rather than a new gate on aqc; the critic's objection to further acquisition gates was that they added no economics, whereas the irreversibility ranking makes a falsifiable prediction about which spending type the uncertainty interaction should penalize most. The three-year horizon is matched across all three budget components, so the ratio is a clean share with a strictly positive denominator.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Flexible Knowledge Investment Under Uncertainty
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(VOL(GROWTH(sale, 1), 5)), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), ADD(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)))))
HYPOTHESIS: When demand is volatile, concentrating the investment budget in research preserves the option to stop, restart, or redirect, and the market underprices this flexibility premium in exactly the firms where it is most valuable.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The parent signal's rank-product form weights high-uncertainty firms in both tails, so it cannot tell us whether the -5.2% alpha comes from shorting committed hard-asset firms or from the long side; reversing only the mix leg isolates that question and, because ranks of complementary shares are not exact negatives of one another, this is a genuinely different sort rather than the same spread relabelled. A confirmed long-side result would also give the archive a second positively signed mechanism with broad coverage.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Externally Financed Hard Investment Mix
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(sstk, DELTA(dltt, 1)), at)), RANK(RATIO(capx, ADD(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Raising outside capital is most damaging when the proceeds are committed to replicable physical capacity rather than to knowledge creation, because investors fund a sunk expansion whose competitive advantage any rival can duplicate.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The archive's oldest joint winner paired external financing with the absence of R&D relative to sales, but the uncertainty result shows the hard-versus-soft budget share is a sharper and better-scaled expression of the same underlying distinction, with no zero-mass problem in the denominator; substituting it tests whether the financing penalty is about lacking knowledge or about where the money goes. This isolates a single well-defined design choice on a mechanism already validated on both metrics.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Growth Option Conversion Into Plant
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), sale)), RANK(GROWTH(ppegt, 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: A research-rich firm that begins a large physical build-out is converting growth options into assets in place, and because the market pays a premium for the option value that the conversion extinguishes, subsequent returns disappoint.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Every conditional in the archive has used low knowledge intensity as the damaging state, so this reverses the conditioning direction and makes the opposite prediction — high knowledge intensity amplifies rather than mitigates the expansion penalty — which means the result is informative regardless of sign and directly tests whether the archive's recurring R&D gate is capturing quality or option value. The interaction is required, since neither research intensity nor plant growth alone identifies the commercialization moment.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Knowledge-Intensive Labor Productivity Gains
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(GROWTH(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), emp), 1)), RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), sale)))
HYPOTHESIS: Rising gross profit per employee at research-intensive firms is evidence that accumulated knowledge capital is being converted into human-capital productivity, a combination the market underprices because neither the research stock nor the productivity gain appears on the balance sheet.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Gross Profit Per Employee Without Plant produced a strong slope of +3.03 but a wrong-signed alpha of -2.2%, and the diagnosis is the second leg: ranking on falling gross plant loads the long portfolio with shrinking, distressed firms whose FF5 exposures turn the spread negative. Replacing the plant-contraction gate with the research-stock gate keeps the human-capital mechanism, removes the distress tilt, and reuses the conditioning variable that carries the archive's only reliable long-side alpha.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---CRITIQUE Hard Capital Stock Under Demand Uncertainty---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A defensible stock-versus-flow reformulation of the archive's best joint result, though ppent/(ppent+R&D stock) collapses to little more than an inverse R&D-intensity rank, so the signal risks being the already-explored "uncertainty × low knowledge" pairing in new clothing rather than a genuine test of capital commitment.

---CRITIQUE Irreversible Acquisitions Under Demand Uncertainty---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Four archived acquisition-gate signals already delivered nearly identical -4.5% to -5.4% alphas with negligible Fama-MacBeth slopes, which is the fingerprint of a single acquirer-underperformance main effect (a well-known published anomaly) rather than an interaction, and the heavily zero-inflated three-year aqc share makes the ranks lumpy and the portfolio composition unstable, so this is likely a fifth draw from the same well.

---CRITIQUE Flexible Knowledge Investment Under Uncertainty---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The stated justification is factually wrong — xrd/(capx+xrd) is a strictly decreasing transform of the parent's capx/(capx+xrd), so its rank is an exact reversal and the only incremental content in the product is the additive uncertainty main effect RANK(VOL), making this a near-mechanical relabelling that cannot decompose the parent's long and short legs as claimed.

---CRITIQUE Externally Financed Hard Investment Mix---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A clean single-variable substitution on a validated mechanism with a better-scaled, zero-mass-free conditioning leg, but the external-financing leg is essentially the published net-external-financing anomaly and the hard/soft mix leg is heavily correlated with the R&D-intensity gate it replaces, so the expected incremental information is modest.

---CRITIQUE Growth Option Conversion Into Plant---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The expected negative sign fights the well-documented positive main effect of R&D intensity, and in an unsigned rank-product that main effect will dominate the spread, so the design cannot separate option-conversion from the R&D anomaly; it is also close to the mirror image of the archived "Plant Contraction With Research Intensification," and "informative regardless of sign" is an admission that the hypothesis is not sharply specified.

---CRITIQUE Knowledge-Intensive Labor Productivity Gains---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: The best-diagnosed proposal here — it correctly identifies the distressed-shrinking-firm tilt as the source of the parent's sign conflict between slope and alpha, and substitutes a conditioning leg with demonstrated long-side alpha while introducing a genuinely new labor-productivity dimension, though it remains cousin to the archive's gross-profit-scaling family and should be checked for overlap with the profitability factor.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Unstable Research Program In A Capital-Heavy Firm
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(VOL(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 5)), RANK(RATIO(ppent, at)))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm that runs its research budget erratically while carrying a heavy sunk physical capital base has neither a credible innovation program nor the flexibility to adapt, and this combination of unreliable intangible investment and rigid tangible commitment predicts low returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This abandons the acquisition channel entirely, accepting the critic's evidence that five draws from that well all recover the same acquirer main effect, and instead moves the second-moment idea to the intangible side, which the archive has never tested — every volatility measure so far has been on capex. It complements rather than repeats Erratic Capex Without Knowledge Anchor, because there instability was measured in the hard channel and the gate was the R&D level, whereas here instability is measured in the knowledge program itself and the gate is the rigidity of the asset base.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Thin Liquidity Against Investment Commitments Under Uncertainty
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(VOL(GROWTH(sale, 1), 5)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(che, ADD(TS_SUM(capx, 3), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3))))))
HYPOTHESIS: Volatile demand is dangerous specifically for firms whose cash reserves are small relative to the scale of the hard and soft investment programs they have committed to, because a revenue trough then forces abandonment of projects at the worst possible time.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: The critic is correct that reversing the mix leg was an exact rank reversal contributing only the uncertainty main effect, so this replaces it with an economically independent second dimension — the liquidity buffer measured against three years of combined tangible and intangible outlays — that supplies the funding mechanism explaining why uncertainty punishes committed investors. It also rehabilitates the cash channel, which failed in Idle Cash Not Converted Into Knowledge because cash was ranked in isolation rather than against the investment obligations it must cover.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Hard Investment Mix Without Pricing Power
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(capx, ADD(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)))), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms that spend their investment budget on replicable physical capacity while lacking any pricing power are adding capital to a business that cannot earn rents on it, and the resulting value destruction is priced only with a lag.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This replaces the poorly specified option-conversion idea, whose predicted sign fought the documented R&D premium, with a sharply signed construct in which both legs point the same way and the interaction is required: a hard investment mix is unremarkable for a firm with a durable margin, and a thin margin is unremarkable for a firm investing in knowledge. It joins the archive's two best-behaved legs for the first time — the hard-versus-soft budget share that carried the -5.2% uncertainty alpha and the sustained-margin moat gate that carried the strongest short-side slope — with full-sample coverage and no zero-mass denominator.
